items.rationale: The frame sustained theft damage, so a like-for-like replacement is covered under 7.1.7(b) and 7.1.9. An estimated €250 gross is reduced to €137.51 by the €500 mobility cap under 4.2.2, using a rateable factor of €500/€909.
The brakes were damaged during the theft, so standard-equivalent replacements are covered under 7.1.7(b) and 7.1.9. The estimated €139 gross is reduced rateably to €76.46 under 4.2.2.
The tracker helped locate the bike, but nothing establishes a separate loss or theft damage to the tracker itself. Sections 4.2.3 and 7.1.5 therefore exclude its replacement.
The second bicycle was unaffected, and routine servicing is independently excluded under 3.1.6 and 7.1.5.
These are additional protective equipment and accessories, with no established loss of or damage to the items they replace. Sections 3.1.7 and 4.2.3 exclude the purchases.

Necessary carriage for the stolen bike's repair is covered under 7.1.7(f), but shipping for the new accessories is not. Assuming this line is repair freight, €25 gross becomes €13.75 under the shared mobility cap.
No separate necessary shop attendance is identified, as required by 7.1.8(f) and 7.1.10. If substantiated, an estimated €25 gross would reduce to about €13.75 under the shared cap.

Fitting the replacement frame and brakes is covered under 7.1.7(c), provided the charge does not duplicate separately billed labour under 7.1.8(g). An estimated €125 gross for distinct fitting work reduces to €68.76 under the shared cap.

Section 7.1.7(e) covers sundries consumed in the theft repair, but 7.1.10 requires allocation away from the unrelated service and purchases. An estimated €8 gross in repair sundries reduces to €4.40 under the shared cap.

Apprentice time is covered under 7.1.7(d) only to the extent it served the theft repair and was not already billed as assembly. One distinct repair hour at €18 gross reduces to €9.90 under the shared cap.

Skilled time attributable to the frame and brake repair is covered under 7.1.7(d), subject to allocation and no duplicate billing. One distinct repair hour at €39 gross reduces to €21.45 under the shared cap.
The initial attendance was necessary to release the bicycle and is separately covered under 5.2.2(a). An estimated €30 gross reduces to €16.50 under the shared mobility cap.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers the lock removal needed to release the recovered bicycle. An estimated €100 gross for the whole two-unit line reduces to €55.01 under 4.2.2.

Sections 5.2.2(a) and 7.1.8(f) cover another attendance only if it was needed for recovery, and no such need is shown. If substantiated, an estimated €30 gross would reduce to about €16.50 under the shared cap.

items.description: Mandatory impound release and storage fee
items.rationale: The yard required payment as a condition of release, so 5.2.2(c) covers €100 plus 19% VAT, or €119 gross. The €1,000 recovery limit does not bind, but the shared €500 mobility cap reduces the line to €65.46.
Sections 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(d) exclude claim processing. Unlike the yard's storage fee, this charge was not a condition of releasing the bicycle.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers every grade of labour needed for lock removal, provided the hour is not already included in the cutting charge. An estimated €18 gross reduces to €9.90 under the shared cap.
Necessary skilled recovery labour is covered under 5.2.2(b), subject to the no-duplication rule in 7.1.8(g). One separately billed hour at €38 gross reduces to €20.90 under the shared cap.
